hot.title: Self-Harness: Harnesses That Improve Themselves
hot.summary: Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory researchers developed Self-Harness, a paradigm allowing a fixed Large Language Model (LLM) agent to autonomously improve its own operating harness by iteratively diagnosing weaknesses, proposing minimal modifications, and validating them. This method achieved significant performance improvements on the Terminal-Bench-2.0 benchmark across various LLMs, demonstrating the generation of targeted, model-specific harness configurations.

hot.title: Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5
Latent Spatial Memory for Video World Models
hot.summary: Mirage introduces a video world model that uses a latent spatial memory to generate 3D-consistent videos, achieving up to 10.57 times faster end-to-end generation and 55 times lower GPU memory usage compared to prior RGB-based memory approaches while enhancing geometric coherence.

hot.title: ICA Lens: Interpreting Language Models Without Training Another Dictionary
hot.summary: Researchers Sida Liu and Feijiang Han introduced ICALens, a workflow that makes Independent Component Analysis practical and efficient for interpreting large language model activations. The method recovers human-interpretable features with high non-Gaussianity and demonstrates competitive utility in sparse probing and targeted probe perturbation tasks compared to existing methods like PCA and some sparse autoencoder variants.

hot.title: FlashMemory-DeepSeek-V4: Lightning Index Ultra-Long Context via Lookahead Sparse Attention
hot.summary: FlashMemory-DeepSeek-V4 implements Lookahead Sparse Attention (LSA) to dynamically manage the Key-Value cache, proactively fetching only query-critical historical chunks. This approach reduces the average GPU memory footprint by 86.5% while improving downstream accuracy by 0.6% on long-context benchmarks.

hot.title: Toward Generalist Autonomous Research via Hypothesis-Tree Refinement
hot.summary: An AI framework named Arbor enables autonomous research by organizing hypotheses, experimental evidence, and insights into a persistent tree structure. This approach allows agents to manage long-horizon scientific tasks and iteratively improve research artifacts more effectively than existing methods.

hot.title: Trajectory-Refined Distillation
hot.summary: Researchers at McGill University, Mila Quebec AI Institute, and UT Austin developed Trajectory-Refined Distillation (TRD) to mitigate 'prefix failure' in on-policy distillation for large language models. TRD refines student-generated trajectories, leading to consistent performance improvements, including up to +4.6% Avg@16 on AIME24 and +12.8% Pass@16 on AMOBench for specific Qwen3 models, while also generating substantially shorter, more verifiable reasoning paths.

hot.title: End-to-End Context Compression at Scale
hot.summary: Latent Context Language Models (LCLMs) offer an encoder-decoder framework for compressing large language model input contexts, enabling efficient handling of millions of tokens. This approach achieved up to an 8.8x faster Time To First Token and substantially reduced peak GPU memory compared to KV cache methods, while preserving high accuracy across diverse long-context tasks.

hot.title: Kwai Keye-VL-2.0 Technical Report
hot.summary: Kuaishou Group's Keye Team developed Kwai Keye-VL-2.0, an open-source Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) multimodal foundation model designed for understanding ultra-long video contexts and enhancing agentic intelligence. The model addresses extreme context scaling and catastrophic forgetting through sparse attention and multi-teacher distillation, achieving leading performance in temporal localization and strong results in various agent tasks.

hot.title: Test-Time Gradient Guidance of Flow Policies in Reinforcement Learning
hot.summary: Researchers from UC Berkeley and Physical Intelligence introduce QGF (Q-Guided Flow), a reinforcement learning algorithm that achieves policy optimization entirely at test time. This method guides a pre-trained flow policy using gradients from a learned Q-function, demonstrating performance competitive with or superior to state-of-the-art training-time RL methods on continuous control tasks, while improving computational efficiency compared to Best-of-N sampling.

hot.title: Breaking Entropy Bounds: Accelerating RL Training via MTP with Rejection Sampling
hot.summary: Bebop, developed by Alibaba's Qwen Team, accelerates large language model reinforcement learning training by enhancing Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) efficiency. It addresses MTP acceptance rate degradation by identifying target model entropy as the dominant factor and introduces an end-to-end Total Variation loss and a pre-RL adaptation strategy, achieving up to 1.8x end-to-end training acceleration.

hot.title: RLCSD: Reinforcement Learning with Contrastive On-Policy Self-Distillation
hot.summary: RLCSD (Reinforcement Learning with Contrastive On-Policy Self-Distillation) enhances the training of large reasoning models by mitigating "privilege-induced style drift" in on-policy self-distillation. The method achieves this by generating a contrastive, task-focused token-level learning signal that is robustly integrated with outcome-level rewards, leading to improved performance and stability on various reasoning tasks.

hot.title: Efficient-WAM: A 1B-Parameter World-Action Model with Low-Cost Future Imagination
hot.summary: Efficient-WAM, a 1-billion-parameter World-Action Model, achieves up to a 32x speedup in inference latency for robot control compared to prior models, enabling real-time deployment while maintaining competitive performance on both simulated and real-world manipulation tasks. The approach demonstrates that photorealistic future visual prediction is not necessary for effective action generation, prioritizing task-relevant dynamic cues instead.

hot.title: Next Forcing: Causal World Modeling with Multi-Chunk Prediction
hot.summary: Next Forcing introduces a multi-chunk prediction framework to enhance causal world models by providing denser temporal supervision, addressing the issue of myopic supervision. It achieves new state-of-the-art performance on robot manipulation tasks, accelerates training by up to 2.3x, and enables 2x inference speedup while improving physical dynamics understanding and general video generation quality.

hot.title: Rethinking the Divergence Regularization in LLM RL
hot.summary: DRPO introduces a novel regularization scheme for large language model reinforcement learning, integrating a divergence-based trust region with smooth quadratic regularization. This approach stabilizes training and improves efficiency, matching or surpassing existing ratio-based and hard-mask methods across diverse LLM architectures and precision environments.

hot.title: InternVideo3: Agentify Foundation Models with Multimodal Contextual Reasoning
hot.summary: InternVideo3, from Shanghai AI Laboratory and Nanjing University, transforms open multimodal models into visually grounded agents for long-horizon reasoning by introducing Multimodal Contextual Reasoning (MCR) and a novel Multimodal Multi-head Latent Attention (M2LA) mechanism. This framework achieves state-of-the-art open-weight performance on several long-video understanding benchmarks and provides up to a 5x decoding speedup for long contexts.

hot.title: i1: A Simple and Fully Open Recipe for Strong Text-to-Image Models
hot.summary: Princeton University researchers systematically investigated over 300 design choices for text-to-image models, leading to i1, a fully open-source model that outperforms previous fully open models by an average of 29.5 absolute percentage points and competes with larger open-weight models.

hot.title: ABot-Earth 0.5: Generative 3D Earth Model
hot.summary: ABot-Earth 0.5, developed by AMAP CV Lab, Alibaba Group, presents a generative 3D Earth model capable of synthesizing vast, real-world-authentic 3D aerial scenes using 3D Gaussian Splatting and conditioned solely on satellite imagery. The model achieves superior generative fidelity with an FID score of 16.1 and KID of 0.006, and can generate 1 km² of 3D environment in under 10 minutes.

hot.title: Reason, Then Re-reason: Cross-view Revisiting Improves Spatial Reasoning
hot.summary: The "Reason, Then Re-reason" (ReRe) framework enables multimodal large language models to improve spatial reasoning from egocentric videos by iteratively verifying initial hypotheses against strategically synthesized novel-view videos. This training-free approach enhances performance on spatial reasoning benchmarks, achieving, for instance, an 8.0% average increase for Qwen3-VL-2B on STI-Bench and allowing open-source models to rival proprietary state-of-the-art models.

hot.title: MotionWAM: Towards Foundation World Action Models for Real-Time Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
hot.summary: A real-time World Action Model, MotionWAM, is introduced for humanoid robots, unifying whole-body control into a single motion latent space for complex loco-manipulation tasks. This approach achieved an overall success rate of 76.1% across nine real-world tasks, outperforming existing baselines by over 32% absolute gain and maintaining a closed-loop operating frequency of 4.9 Hz.

likes.title: Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5
Paving the way for agents in biology
On the Geometry of On-Policy Distillation
likes.summary: Researchers at HKUST, UT Austin, Zhejiang University, and others characterized the parameter-space optimization geometry of On-Policy Distillation (OPD) for large language models, finding it occupies a "relaxed off-principal" regime distinct from SFT and RLVR. OPD exhibits "subspace locking" where cumulative updates rapidly converge into a low-dimensional, functionally sufficient channel, primarily controlled by the objective's composition.

likes.title: LARA: Latent Action Representation Alignment for Vision-Language-Action Models
likes.summary: The LARA (Latent Action Representation Alignment) framework jointly optimizes Latent Action Models (LAMs) and Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models by explicitly aligning their intermediate latent representations. This approach enhances VLA model performance and generalization capabilities across various robotic manipulation benchmarks, achieving improved success rates and better adaptation to novel tasks and embodiments.

likes.title: ConMem: Structured Memory-Guided Adaptation in Training-Free Multi-Agent Systems
likes.summary: ConMem presents a training-free framework for multi-agent systems to achieve continual adaptation by transforming fragmented experiences into structured, coordinated collective memory. It leverages signed strategy cards and a typed graph to provide prompt-side guidance, consistently yielding 10.9% to 12.9% absolute performance gains across diverse benchmarks and host LLM architectures.

likes.title: dots.tts Technical Report
likes.summary: The "dots.tts" system, developed by researchers at dots, Xiaohongshu Inc. and Shanghai Jiao Tong University, introduces a 2B-parameter continuous autoregressive text-to-speech foundation model designed to overcome long-range error accumulation in continuous latent generation. It achieves high fidelity and robust zero-shot voice cloning, outperforming baselines in speaker similarity and text faithfulness while enabling efficient real-time inference.

likes.title: Echo-Memory: A Controlled Study of Memory in Action World Models
likes.summary: A controlled study by researchers from various institutions systematically compared different memory mechanisms in action world models, demonstrating that traditional replay metrics are insufficient for assessing a model's capacity to preserve consistent scene and object identity across camera revisits. The study revealed distinct performance trade-offs among memory families using a new three-branch evaluation protocol.

likes.title: AHA-WAM:Asynchronous Horizon-Adaptive World-Action Modeling with Observation-Guided Context Routing
likes.summary: AHA-WAM introduces an asynchronous, horizon-adaptive architecture for robot manipulation, decoupling the temporal scales of visual world planning and action execution. This approach achieves a 4.59x inference speedup and a 24.17 Hz control frequency (up to 56.95 Hz with distillation), while maintaining a 92.80% success rate on RoboTwin 2.0 tasks and 78.33% on real-world tasks.

likes.title: Watch, Remember, Reason: Human-View Video Understanding with MLLMs
likes.summary: A comprehensive survey introduces the 'watch, remember, reason' human-view taxonomy to structure and integrate multimodal large language model methods for long, knowledge-intensive video understanding. This framework clarifies functional roles across perception, memory, and reasoning, guiding the analysis of current advancements and future research directions.

likes.title: SWE-Explore: Benchmarking How Coding Agents Explore Repositories
likes.summary: SWE-Explore introduces a benchmark specifically designed to evaluate how coding agents explore code repositories at a fine-grained, line-level. It reveals that while current agents are effective at identifying relevant files, they struggle to precisely pinpoint all necessary lines of code for a fix, identifying a key bottleneck in automated software engineering. The benchmark's upstream metrics for exploration showed strong correlation with downstream bug-fixing success.

likes.title: MilliVid: Hierarchical Latents for Long-Range Consistency in Video Generation
likes.summary: MILLIVID, a video generative model, enhances long-range consistency by employing a learned hierarchical tokenizer and a coarse-to-fine rollout strategy. It produces videos with significantly improved object permanence and scene recall over hundreds of frames, demonstrating superior performance on consistency metrics like LPIPS (0.335 vs 0.533 for FramePack) and LightGlue matches (62.4 vs 7.0 for FramePack) while maintaining visual quality.
